title: Naming conventions
text:
Lines, crosses, seedlots and traits all follow set naming patterns. Consistent names are what let Breedbase link records, let us find seed and data years later, and let anyone in the lab read a name and know what it refers to.






Important



If something doesn’t fit these conventions, ask before creating a new code or format.

title: Contributing
text: Anyone in the lab can edit this site. Small fixes can be made in the browser on GitHub. Bigger changes are easier on your own computer.

title: Contributing
text:
Quick fix in the browser
Click Edit this page (under the table of contents on the right) on any page. GitHub opens the source file. Make the change and open a pull request. The site rebuilds after the pull request is merged into main.

title: Contributing
text:
Working on your own computer

Install Quarto. RStudio and Positron already include it.
Clone this repository.
From the repository folder, run:

quarto preview
The site opens in your browser and reloads every time you save a file.

title: Contributing
text:
Adding a page

Copy _templates/page.qmd into the folder for the section it belongs in, for example protocols/fruit-firmness.qmd. Use lowercase file names with hyphens.
Fill in title, description, and order at the top of the file.
Save. The page appears in the sidebar on its own. You do not need to edit _quarto.yml.

To add a whole new section, make a new folder containing an index.qmd. That page’s title becomes the sidebar heading, and its order sets where the section appears.

title: Contributing
text:
Images
Put images in an images/ folder inside the section and always write alt text. See Quarto syntax for the format.

title: Contributing
text:
Pages that run code
If a page runs R or Python code, render it on your computer before pushing (quarto render path/to/page.qmd) and commit the _freeze/ folder along with your page. The GitHub build reuses those stored results and never runs your code, so it does not need R, Python, or your packages.

title: Contributing
text:
Submitting changes
git switch -c fix-nextcloud-page     # new branch
# ...edit, preview, save...
git add .
git commit -m "Update Nextcloud folder structure"
git push -u origin fix-nextcloud-page
Then open a pull request on GitHub. Once it is merged into main, the site publishes in a few minutes.

title: Contributing
text:
Writing guidelines

One topic per page.
Write steps that someone new can follow without asking you.
Link to the source of truth (Breedbase, a pipeline’s own repository) instead of copying details that change.
If a step has a common failure, add a Troubleshooting section rather than burying it in the steps.

text:
Running R code
A chunk with {r} runs when the page renders and shows its output. Remove engine: markdown from the page header if you add one, and commit _freeze/ afterwards (see Contributing).
```{r}
#| label: fig-yield
#| fig-cap: "Fruit weight by entry"
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(pheno, aes(entry, fruit_wt)) + geom_boxplot()
```

title: Breeding nomenclature
text: This page covers the parts every code is built from, with a quick reference of example IDs. The pages that follow explain each type in detail.

title: Breeding nomenclature
text:
Building blocks
New IDs for breeding material are based off of the table below.










Part
Abbreviation
Format
Meaning
Example




Year
[YY]
2 digits
Year of the season (see below)
27


Season
[S]
1 digit
1 = winter, 2 = summer, 3 = fall
2


Accession type
H or F
1 letter, or nothing
Nothing = elite inbred, H = elite hybrid, F = family
H


Market class
[MC]
2 or 3 letters
From the controlled vocabulary
PU


Counter
[####]
4 digits, zero-padded
Sequence number within the year
0005




Year and season
The year and season part of the code is used to provide information on when material is derived. See specific rules below.

A winter season that crosses New Year takes the year it ends: December 2026 to March 2027 is 271.
This keeps codes in calendar order: 262 (summer 2026), 271 (winter 2026 to 2027), 272 (summer 2027), 273 (fall 2027, late-summer finished before the New Year).

What the year and season record depends on the code:



Accession Type
Year and season record




Elite inbred or hybrid
First season the line was in an elite trial


Family prefix
First season the F1 seed was planted


Cross ID
Year only: the year the cross was made





Market class

2 or 3 letters, from the controlled vocabulary. 
No 3-letter code may start with H or F. Otherwise 262HUB0001 could be an elite inbred of class HUB or an elite hybrid of class UB.



Counter

Counts per market class, per year. It does not restart between seasons: if 271PU0003 exists, the next pumpkin inbred coded in 2027 is 0004, whether that’s in summer (272PU0004) or fall (273PU0004).
Inbreds, hybrids and families keep separate counters. 272PU0005, 272HPU0005 and 272FPU0005 can all exist and are unrelated.

title: Breeding nomenclature
text:
Quick reference









Material
Pattern
Example
Reads as




Cross
[YY][trial]X[###]
23HCX001
1st cross in the 23HC crossing trial


Test cross
[YY][trial]X[###]

A cross made in a trial with TC in its name


F1 family
[YY][S]F[MC][####]-#
232FAC0001-1
F1 from cross 23HCX001; first planted summer 2023


Selfed generations
-# per selfed plant
232FAC0001-1-5-6-8
F4: plants 5, 6, then 8 selfed


Plot bulk
-P#
232FAC0001-1-P8
F2 seed bulked from plot 8 of F1 plants


Fruit
F# after the plant or plot
232FAC0001-1-5-6-8F2
Seed from fruit 2 of selfed plant 8


Hybrid-derived family
-H-# instead of -#
242FPU0001-H-1
Selfed commercial hybrid (cross 24PUX001); treat as an F2


Backcross
-BF# or -BM#
231FPU0001-1-BM5-BM10-BM6-7
Three backcrosses to the male parent, then one self


Elite inbred
[YY][S][MC][####]
272PU0005
5th pumpkin inbred coded in 2027; first elite trial summer 2027


Elite hybrid
[YY][S]H[MC][####]
232HPU0010
10th pumpkin hybrid coded in 2023; first elite trial summer 2023


Shared seed
NH + elite code
NH272PU0005
272PU0005 as sent outside the program


Seedlot (non-commercial)
[accession]_[trial]-[plot]-[plant]-[fruit]
PuritanBN_15881_242INCBLK4-019-1
Plant 1, plot 19, trial 242INCBLK4; plant and fruit are optional


Seedlot (commercial)
[accession]_[YY]C[#]
Spicy_Mocha_23C1
First Spicy_Mocha packet received in 2023
